idiom_name: go/ast node types plus type switches, with astutil.Apply Cursor for rewriting
implementation_notes: The tree comes from go/parser, and the matcher is an ordinary type switch over ast.Node - case *ast.CallExpr with a further assertion on x.Fun and a name check - so a pattern is structure checking in Go rather than a separate notation. go/ast.Inspect (or the go1.23 iterator Preorder, or PreorderStack when the enclosing stack matters) owns a depth-first walk; rewriting needs golang.org/x/tools/go/astutil.Apply, whose Cursor carries the parent so it can Replace, Delete, InsertBefore or InsertAfter a node, which Inspect cannot do because it hands nodes out by value. For many analyses over one file, golang.org/x/tools/go/ast/inspector materialises the traversal stack and filters by node type, and the go/analysis framework packages the rules for shipping.
pitfalls: ast.Inspect hands you the node value, so you cannot replace the node itself; using it for rewriting silently only mutates children and leaves the matched node in place.

A type switch that misses a variant compiles and never matches, and a shape wrapped by parents (a CallExpr inside a ParenExpr inside an ExprStmt) is not visible unless the rule recurses into the wrapper.

Nodes carry positions resolved through the token.FileSet; a replacement built from scratch has NoPos and breaks comment attachment and formatting, so reuse original positions and run go/format over the result.
